thread:
maya: Hey all — quick follow-up from last night's latency surge. We need PRD updates for graceful degradation + runbook additions. Link to incident: https://redwood.inc/incident/1752099. Can we align on acceptance criteria and launch gates by EOD Wed? :wave:

rajan: +1. From SRE perspective main asks: 1) automatic fallback to cheaper model within 200ms of detection, 2) circuit-breaker that trips at 5% error rate over 1m, 3) clear metric to track (p95 tail latency for API). I'll add specifics to the runbook draft. cc @ellie

ellie: Implementation constraints: switching models must preserve prompt context; we have ~120ms for KV repopulation if we warm caches. If fallback replaces model we need an API flag `X-fallback-reason`. Also quantized variants cause hallucination differences — acceptance criteria must include quality check (embedding distance) or we risk regressions.

tom: Customers are asking for guarantee: "no silent failure" — they'd rather fail closed than return low-quality. We should add opt-in "strict-quality" route that blocks fallback and returns 503s instead. Could be part of roadmap for Dedicated tier.

incident-bot: Incident 1752099: Latency surge detected 2025-03-03T01:14Z. Auto-scaling delays observed. See timeline: deploy 01:03Z -> spike 01:12Z -> mitigation 01:45Z.

maya: Good point, @tom. Let's include two launch audiences in PRD: default (auto-fallback enabled) and strict-quality customers (opt-in). Acceptance criteria candidate list: default and strict routes must have explicit gates, quality regression < 2% on core prompts, and runbook entries added.

rajan: Proposed SLOs for rollout gating: p95 < 350ms on normal; fallback route p95 < 450ms. Rollout condition: <1% fallback rate in canary for 24h. Also add a throttling guard in the routing layer: don't route >10 qps per model shard if under duress.

ellie: Edge cases: long-running streaming sessions, function calling with external tools — fallback should not break tool invocations. We'll add "no tool-fallback" rule in runbook and a fallback-safe API flag `disable_fallback_tools=true`.

maya: Who owns PRD edits? I'll take initial draft. @rajan can you paste the runbook snippet you mentioned? We should embed it in doc and link to the PRD.

rajan: Runbook snippet:

```
Runbook excerpt - fallback detection
if error_rate_1m > 5% OR p95_latency > 500ms:
  set routing.policy = "fallback_preferred"
  notify #eng-oncall + pageduty
  if fallback_rate > 10% for 15m: revert to degraded mode + notify PMs
```

ellie: I'll add acceptance tests: synthetic quality checks (embedding cosine > 0.92) + smoke tests that assert tool calls still succeed. Also CI step to run small prompt regression suite before enabling fallback by default.

tom: Add customer communication checklist: email template + status page update + toggle UI for dedicated customers. We need copy approved by legal for downstream risk statements.

maya: Plan: I'll update PRD draft today, include acceptance criteria, risk matrix, and rollout gates. Target PRD review on Thu 11am PT. After that, eng will prototype fallback routing and SRE will add runbook items. If anyone wants to add items, drop them here or edit: https://redwood.docs/prd/fallback-degradation (do not forget to add owners).

ellie: ack. I'll schedule eng sync post-review.

rajan: ack from SRE. I'll create the runbook ticket and link to PRD.

incident-bot: Note: New runbook entry created: RB-452. Created by rajan.
